input.title: Two Similar Transfers
input.request: Mira, the account holder, wants H&V to establish whether two similar outgoing transfer entries are one instruction shown twice or two separate instructions, and asks whether the second can be stopped or returned.

events.text: Your payment activity shows two similar outgoing transfer entries to North Quay Utilities for £84.20. One is marked Completed and the other Pending.
I own this account and only meant to make one transfer. Please check whether these are separate instructions, and whether the pending one has been stopped or returned.
I’m checking the count and independent instruction references for Mira’s own payment instructions before advising. I have not cancelled or returned either instruction.

summary: Mira Ellison, writing unverified over secure chat, asked whether two similar transfers were separate instructions and whether the pending one had been stopped or returned. The desk classed it as a transfer query with a payment question, found that the payment system had already been asked but no answer was in the case, and closed it in WAITING with the outcome "wait". Nothing was stopped, returned or cancelled, and the agent's later attempts to query the payment system again and to escalate to a person were both refused because the case was no longer in the right state, so no one has been handed it. What is left is for a person to verify her identity, check the payment records for a duplicate, and decide on the pending or completed transfer.

She says only one was intended and asks whether they are separate instructions and whether the pending one can be stopped or returned. The payment system was already asked (payment_asked=True) but no answer is in the case, and a new payment query was refused because the case is in WAITING. Do not claim a result before the records show it.

Questions:
- request_type (choice): What does the customer want from the bank now?
    status: the stage or status of a payment, card, file, device or request
    reason: why something was declined, restricted or did not run
    record_fact: a detail from a record (a date, a purpose, an amount, a limit, a fee, a mandate, active instructions)
    register: a dispute, a review, a correction or a return to be looked into by a team

    authority: something only another person may approve or give (a second signatory, an administrator, a new user's access)

    transfer: an outgoing transfer or payment the customer made, or a payment instruction
    incoming_payment: money expected into the customer's account, or a refund to it
    standing_order: a standing order or a recurring payment instruction
    direct_debit: a Direct Debit mandate or collection
    card: a card itself (replacement, dispatch, block, restriction, PIN)
    card_payment: a card purchase or card payment attempt
    batch: an uploaded payment or payroll file, or a row in it
    payment_package: a payment package waiting for signatories
    profile: the customer's profile details (name, phone, address)
    access: signing in, devices, sessions, password recovery
    statement: an account statement
    document: an export, a report or a bank confirmation document
    fee: a fee or charge applied by the bank
    limit: a payment limit
    role: a user's role or access in a company profile
